belief: I have to clean up my life before I can come to God.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that you have to clean up your life before you can come to God, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Feeling too ashamed or messy to approach God. Church cultures where people seemed to have it all together. Believing God only welcomes the good. Trying and failing to fix yourself first. Fear of rejection by God or His people.
teaches: Jesus came for sinners, not for people who already have it all together. While we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly. The prodigal son came home in rags, and his father ran to embrace him before he could clean up. Jesus said, “Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened.” God invites you to reason with Him: though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow. You come as you are, and He does the cleaning.
self_statements: I need to get my life together first.
God won’t accept me as I am.
Once I stop this habit, I’ll come back to God.
I have to earn my way back.
God only wants people who have it together.
errors: Believing change must come before coming to God, instead of through Him.
Calling yourself too messy or too far gone.
Staying away from God out of fear of rejection.
Trying to fix yourself before letting God help.
questions: What did the father do before the prodigal could clean up?
When did Christ die for the ungodly?
Who does Jesus invite to come to Him?
Can I clean myself up without God’s help?
What does Isaiah 1:18 say God will do with my sins?
Am I waiting for something God never asked me to do first?
What would it look like to come to God as I am today?
truth: I do not have to clean up my life before I can come to God. Jesus came for sinners. The Father runs to meet me as I am. I come with my mess, and He forgives and cleanses me. Change follows coming to God; it is not the price of admission.
hw_questions: What did the father do before the son cleaned up?
When did Christ die for the ungodly?
Can I clean myself up without God?
What will God do with my sins?
What would coming as I am look like today?
hw_truths: I can come to God as I am.
The Father runs to meet me.
Christ died for me while I was powerless.
God cleanses me; I don’t clean myself.
Jesus invites all who are weary and burdened.
log: Each day, write one honest thing I brought to God without cleaning it up first.
name_example: So Sarah got up and went to her Father. But while she was still in the distance, her Father saw her and was filled with compassion. He ran to her, embraced her, and kissed her.
actions: Pray today exactly as you are,
telling God honestly about your mess.
and write what the son had planned to say and what the father did instead.
Go to church or call a believer this week
Ask God for help with one area of change,
trusting Him to do the work with you.
tracker: One thing I brought to God as I am
prayer: Father, thank You that I can come to You just as I am. Help me reject the lie that I have to clean up my life first. I come to You with my mess, trusting You to forgive me, cleanse me, and change me from the inside. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
